questions.q: Let $\mathbf{u}=\langle2,-1,3\rangle$, $\mathbf{v}=\langle1,4,-2\rangle$. Find $\mathbf{u}+\mathbf{v}$ and $3\mathbf{u}-2\mathbf{v}$.
For $\mathbf{u}=\langle1,2,2\rangle$, $\mathbf{v}=\langle3,-1,0\rangle$, find $\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v}$ and $|\mathbf{u}|$.
Find the angle between $\mathbf{u}=\langle1,0,0\rangle$ and $\mathbf{v}=\langle1,1,0\rangle$ using $\cos\theta=\dfrac{\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v}}{|\mathbf{u}||\mathbf{v}|}$.
State the Cauchy–Schwarz Inequality.
Verify the Cauchy–Schwarz Inequality for $\mathbf{u}=\langle3,4\rangle$, $\mathbf{v}=\langle1,2\rangle$.
questions.answer: $\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v}=3+8=11$. $|\mathbf{u}|=5$, $|\mathbf{v}|=\sqrt5$, so $|\mathbf{u}||\mathbf{v}|=5\sqrt5\approx11.18$. Since $11 \le 11.18$, the inequality holds (it is strict here because $\mathbf{u}$ and $\mathbf{v}$ are not parallel).

questions.q: Find the unit vector in the direction of $\mathbf{v}=\langle3,-4\rangle$.
Determine whether $\mathbf{u}=\langle2,-3,1\rangle$ and $\mathbf{v}=\langle1,2,4\rangle$ are orthogonal.
questions.answer: $\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v}=2(1)+(-3)(2)+1(4)=2-6+4=0$. Since the dot product is $0$, they are orthogonal.

sections.heading: Distance between two points as a vector norm

questions.q: Find the distance between $P(1,2,3)$ and $Q(4,-1,5)$ using $|\overrightarrow{PQ}|$.
Write $\mathbf{w}=\langle7,4\rangle$ as a linear combination $a\mathbf{u}+b\mathbf{v}$ of $\mathbf{u}=\langle1,0\rangle$ and $\mathbf{v}=\langle0,1\rangle$.
questions.answer: $\mathbf{w}=7\mathbf{u}+4\mathbf{v}$, i.e. $a=7$, $b=4$ (the standard basis vectors, so the coefficients are just $\mathbf{w}$'s own components).

questions.q: Write $\mathbf{w}=\langle5,1\rangle$ as a linear combination $a\mathbf{u}+b\mathbf{v}$ of $\mathbf{u}=\langle1,1\rangle$ and $\mathbf{v}=\langle1,-1\rangle$.
questions.answer: Need $a+b=5$ and $a-b=1$. Adding: $2a=6\Rightarrow a=3$; then $b=2$. So $\mathbf{w}=3\mathbf{u}+2\mathbf{v}$. Check: $3\langle1,1\rangle+2\langle1,-1\rangle=\langle3,3\rangle+\langle2,-2\rangle=\langle5,1\rangle$. ✓

questions.q: Find the vector $\overrightarrow{PQ}$ from $P(2,-1,0)$ to $Q(5,3,-2)$.
Find $|\overrightarrow{PQ}|$ for the vector found above.
For $\mathbf{v}=\langle2,-3\rangle$, is $-4\mathbf{v}$ in the same direction as $\mathbf{v}$, or the opposite?
questions.answer: Since $-4<0$, $-4\mathbf{v}=\langle-8,12\rangle$ points in the opposite direction to $\mathbf{v}$ (and is $4$ times as long).

questions.q: Are $\mathbf{u}=\langle2,-6\rangle$ and $\mathbf{v}=\langle-1,3\rangle$ parallel?
questions.answer: $\mathbf{u}=-2\mathbf{v}$ (check: $-2\langle-1,3\rangle=\langle2,-6\rangle$ ✓), so yes — $\mathbf{u}$ and $\mathbf{v}$ are parallel (scalar multiples of each other).

questions.q: Find the midpoint $M$ of the segment from $P(1,-2,3)$ to $Q(5,4,-1)$, using $M=\dfrac{1}{2}(P+Q)$ (averaging componentwise).

sections.heading: Normalizing a vector to a given length

questions.q: Find the vector of length $10$ in the same direction as $\mathbf{v}=\langle3,4\rangle$.
questions.answer: $|\mathbf{v}|=5$, so the unit vector is $\left\langle\dfrac35,\dfrac45\right\rangle$. Scaling to length $10$: $10\left\langle\dfrac35,\dfrac45\right\rangle=\langle6,8\rangle$.
